facts.label: Comparativos com expectativa
facts.sub: better / worse / -er / more + adjetivo + than I expected. Para viagem passada, use was/were e expected no passado.

facts.label: Melhor do que
facts.sub: Better é o comparativo de good. Use better than para dizer que algo superou a sua ideia: The view was better than I expected. Nunca diga more good ou more better.

facts.label: Pior do que
facts.sub: Worse é o comparativo de bad. Use para expectativas que não se realizaram: The weather was worse than I expected. Atenção: worse não é worser, e worst é o superlativo.

paragraphs: It is a bright Sunday afternoon in Liverpool. Theo has just come back from a walk by the river. He meets his friend Felix at a small cafe. Felix did not go because he was ill. Now he wants to hear everything about the day. Theo compares the trip with his plans.

“Theo, how was the trip to the seafront? Was it good?” says Felix. “The view was better than I expected. The river was wide and blue.” says Theo. “Really? I thought the weather would be worse than it was last year.” says Felix.
